summary: Build the moduli-specific algebra of tautological rings and semi-tautological extensions, its finite-generation and boundary-induction tools, and the geometric Chow–Kunneth arguments needed in genus seven. Plan the cusp-decorated graph calculations and realization classification in degrees thirteen, fourteen and fifteen, with explicit proof gates for descent, stack comparisons and finite computational certificates.

nodes.title: Tautological Chow and cohomology rings
nodes.statement: For all stable pairs take the least system of unital graded rational Chow subalgebras R*(Mbar_g, n) closed under proper forgetting and clutching pushforward and the corresponding defined pullbacks and relabellings. The usual equivalent decorated-stable-graph description uses marking psi classes, vertex kappa classes and gluing. Put R*(M_g, n)=image of restriction and RH*=image under the cycle map. Cohomological degree is twice Chow codimension.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: Intersect all such systems; the full Chow system supplies existence. Use the graph calculus, projection and excess formulas to compare the closure and graph descriptions; the stack cycle realization is an explicit supplier obligation.

nodes.title: The stable-pair induction order
nodes.statement: For pairs of natural numbers define (g′, n′)≺(g, n) iff g′≤g, 2g′+n′≤2g+n, and the pairs differ. Restrict to 2g−2+n>0 when using moduli. Use integer d=3g−3+n. The order is well founded by lexicographic descent of (g,2g+n).
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: If genus stays equal, the second coordinate strictly decreases; otherwise genus strictly decreases. For a stable graph, the genus formula and stability show each vertex pair is smaller than the total whenever the graph has an edge.
acceptance: (0,4)≺(1,2), although both have2g+n=4.
(1,2) does not precede(0,4).
(1,1) does not precede itself; the unstable pair(0,2) is excluded from moduli induction.

nodes.title: The filling criterion
nodes.statement: Let S be an STE and fix stable(g, n), k≥0. Suppose S^q(Mbar_g′, n′) surjects onto W_qH^q(M_g′, n′)/(Phi^q+RH^q) for the current triple and every stable smaller pair, 0≤q≤k, with 2d′−q≤2d−k. Then S^k(Mbar_g, n)=H^k(Mbar_g, n). proofSteps: Induct on the stable-pair order. The enlarged hypotheses pass to every boundary Künneth factor of degree≤k−2 and to every stable forgetful source in the same degree k. nodes.title: Casnati–Ekedahl pushforward is tautological
nodes.statement: For any genus g≥2 in the tetragonal construction, define the same Hurwitz stack with rank 3 E and rank 2 F both of degree g+3. A class in the image A*((P E dual)^n)→A*(H^diamond_4, g, n) pushes forward under the proper forgetting map to a tautological class on M_g, n minus its gonality≤3 locus. The genus-seven instance has degree 10.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: Expand in the projective hyperplane classes and Chern classes of E, F; push along the cover incidence and use GRR to express the resulting classes in kappa, psi and Hodge classes. The exact nodal/stack GRR and Hurwitz-source inputs remain supplier contracts.
acceptance: A statement merely asserting all classes are algebraic would not give the required tautological pushforward.

nodes.title: Universal maximal-isotropic Chow generation
nodes.statement: For a split nondegenerate10-dimensional quadratic space over C, fix one connected component OG+(5,10). The quotient[OG+/SO10] is BP for its maximal-isotropic parabolic, with Levi GL5 and split unipotent radical of dimension 10. It has CKgP and rational Chow ring Q[c1(U),…, c5(U)]. On BP the standard quadratic bundle fits0→U→V→U dual→0; do not require an equivariant direct-sum splitting.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: Identify the parabolic and its Levi; the map BGL5→BP is the unipotent affine-bundle comparison. Apply homotopy invariance, obtaining the polynomial Chern presentation. The nonsplit representation extension suffices for Chern identities.
acceptance: The relative dimension is10.
The disconnected union of both isotropic components is not the fixed component of the spinor embedding.

nodes.title: Mukai central lift and moduli comparison
nodes.statement: For the smooth pentagonal genus-seven linear-section incidence I_n in the spinor embedding OG+⊂P(S+), S+ has rank 16 and the action is Spin10, not SO10. Construct[I_n/Spin10] and its central rigidification by the projectively ineffective Z(Spin10)=mu4. Prove the comparison of the resulting effective quotient[I_n/PSO10] with the actual stack M^circle_7, n, preserving precisely curve automorphism groups and all marking-forgetting maps. A residual gerbe description must name its band and any remaining stabilizers.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: Use Mukai’s canonical construction W=ker(Sym²H0(omega)→H0(omega²)), rank 10 with its quadratic structure, and the rank 5 kernels from omega(−p). Prove the family comparison and full faithfulness including automorphisms. Existing half-spin algebra supplies only the representation; the central quotient and curve-family comparison are unproved gates G-mukai, not conclusions of the printed SO quotient.

nodes.title: Marked spinor incidence model
nodes.statement: On the Spin10 lift, let Z_n⊂(OG+)^n be the locus where the sum of the n tautological lines injects into S+. Put Q_n=coker(⊕L_i→S+), rank 16−n. For 0≤n≤4 use the subspace Grassmannian Gr^sub_(7−n)(Q_n), equivalently the supplier’s rank-nine quotient Grassmannian Gr_9(Q_n). Its universal kernel E_n has rank 7−n; its inverse image in S+ is the desired rank-seven subbundle containing the marked lines. Remove the nonsmooth-section locus. Gonality5 ensures independence of the marked canonical points. Transfer to M^circle_7, n requires both Mukai gates; the orthogonal fibre-power Chow argument applies only for n≥1.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
proofSteps: Form the open rank locus and actual quotient bundle upstairs, then the relative Grassmannian and smooth complete-intersection open. Apply the separately proved stack comparison; do not identify a generic Grassmann quotient with curve moduli without it.
acceptance: n=0 gives Gr^sub_7(16)≅Gr_9(16), with universal quotient rank9.
n=4 gives rankQ=12, rankE=3 and quotient rank9.
A repeated point has dependent lines and lies outside Z_n.

nodes.title: Canonical genus-four quadric incidence families

V^type_n parametrizes the equation plus n ordered distinct points lying on it; C^type_n is its universal complete-intersection curve, including singular and nonreduced fibres for the sieve.

proofSteps: Apply canonical genus-four Petri geometry and classify reduced irreducible quadrics over finite fields, including characteristic2. The cone’s vertex condition selects an affine chart; the other equations are sections of O(3,3).

nodes.title: Cone sieve coefficients
nodes.statement: For 0≤n, d≤3 the signed sieve coefficient S_d(C^cone_n) is the polynomial in the attached table, with p_r=1+q+…+q^r and qj meaning q^j. For the split marked rows, displayed S2, S3 and the n=3 S1 are their degree≥6 polynomial part with error o(q6) as q grows through prime powers; unmarked rows and the other marked S0, S1 formulas are exact. Cone and nonsplit tables are exact.
hypotheses: Standing coefficient, stability and dimension conventions in the reader apply; additional restrictions are in the statement.
